player_base.design_purpose: Baseline survivability before any equipment. armour_reduction_scale controls how fast armour approaches full physical reduction (reduction = armour / (armour + scale)); resistance_cap_percent stops resistance stacking from trivialising elemental threats.

shelter.design_purpose: Resting in a shelter is the health-regeneration route (owner playtest 2 Sep 2026: 'you need some passive health regeneration or a way to get health regened'). A shelter is an enclosed room - the sim flood-fills the space around the player through open cells, stopped by placed walls, floors, blocks and by terrain, and it is a shelter when the fill closes before max_room_cells build cells without reaching open sky. Regen starts settle_rounds after the last hit taken and pays regen_life_per_round (per round_seconds of combat_realtime.json), so a hut is worth building on day one, a dug-out hollow with a slab over its mouth counts, and a mob that breaks in stops the rest. Out in the open, nothing regenerates: the deprivation the owner asked for at the start stays. max_room_cells is a cost guard, not a house size (owner playtest 3 Sep 2026: an enclosed house did not count - 96 cells is a 6x6x3 room and a real house is bigger): 400 build cells is a hall, and the sky is what says a room is open.

day.design_purpose: Owner revision, 5 Sep 2026: exposure_life_per_round is zero, disabling nighttime health drain for now. Lighting, enemy wake ranges and shelter healing remain. The following describes the optional exposure controls and original intent; exposure is currently off. Day and night (Wave 6 slice 5; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: 'imperative there is almost like a forced - go back and continue your shelter, and get lost in that for a bit'). A day is length_seconds of play (twelve minutes); a new game starts start_fraction into day one so the first day is long; the phases end at dawn_end, day_end and dusk_end as fractions of the day, so the night is the last third - about four minutes, long enough to build through. Dusk is the warning: the light goes, the HUD counts down and points home. Night: the world keeps night_light of its daylight; out in the open the cold takes exposure_life_per_round per round of combat_realtime.json down to exposure_floor_fraction of max life and no further (it never kills; it sends you home); packs wake from night_aggro_multiplier times as far and stay awake night_sleep_range_multiplier times as far; in a shelter the rest pays shelter_night_regen_multiplier times the shelter's regen. The night is the forced return: the open is worse, the roof is better, and the four minutes are for the shelter.

hauling.design_purpose: INT-03D (8 Sep 2026): ordinary timber, field/split/dressed stone and the eight habitat ingredients/finishes carry 240 units each, enough for a measured 188-wood six-metre home plus its workshop and staging chest (225 wood total). A mineral haul refines into 120 finished units; reed/log hauls into 240. chest_units is shared across all contents: 960 stores four full common stacks. These values reduce hauling interruptions, not trees, finite stock, recipe costs or refinement losses. carry_cap applies per family to ground pickup and chest withdrawal; unlisted items retain carry_cap_default 40, wedges 40, hide/ores 30 and curios 1. Equipment bases remain uncapped. Crafting and death/trial recovery preserve every output even above a hauling cap, as do existing saves. Full families leave pickup remainders on the ground. E at a placed chest moves exact quantities; dismantling spills all contents. Machine buffers and source budgets are separate and unchanged. See docs/prototype/building-loads-2026-09-08.md for the measured candidate and remaining comfort review.

siege.design_purpose: The siege (Wave 7 slice 3; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: the house cycle needs the night to test it). From first_night on, each night rolls chance_per_night from the world seed and the day (a save replays its nights). On a siege night the dusk notice carries the howl, and arrive_seconds_into_night later - if you are within home_radius_m of the shelter you last rested in - the era's pack (pack_by_era, the highest era at or under the current) takes shape spawn_radius_m out in the dark around home, hunting from the start. They circle, they scratch at what they press against (the house shakes and says so), and they are gone with the dawn. In the valley a shut timber door holds. Once the deep wakes the husk breaks timber (eras.json breaks_timber): after timber_break_hits scratches a timber piece gives, so the hut becomes stone - the masonry unlock earning its keep. Stone and iron never give. Not on the first night: the first night is for learning the dark.

enemies.design_purpose: Basic fodder that teaches area clearing
Introduces fire damage in small doses before the boss
Cheap but quick; the hastened weakness makes packs of these frightening
Slow hill guardian that makes stone and iron country feel owned; killing it IS mining, so combat feeds construction directly

The aggro-chainer (D-012, named in the roadmap): it hangs back and SCREAMS - every idle mob in scream radius joins the chase, so a pack with a shrieker recruits the biome. Kill it first or fight everything it can see. Barely dangerous alone; its page chance is the bounty on its head.
The cave dweller: quick in the tunnels where there is no room to kite, guarding the underground iron. Meeting one in the dark is the cost of the richer veins.
The fen's wall: slow, thick, and it does not bleed (nothing to open in that hide). You do not train a lurker, you walk around it - and a wisp behind it makes the walk cost.
The fen's sting: a fast skirmisher that keeps its distance and pecks. Alone it is a nuisance; behind a lurker it is the reason to bring a projectile.

The wastes' skirmisher: burning, quick, ignite-proof, and fire barely marks a thing made of it (damage_taken fire 0.25, D-023 slice 2; the owner: heavily reduced, not immune - a two-element hit lands its other packet whole and a quarter of its fire). It is what makes fire resistance matter outside the trial, and the first mob an all-fire plate must find a second element for.

The wastes' armoured line: slow, heavy, and fire does little to a hollow suit - it will not burn (immune_statuses) and takes a quarter of a fire hit (damage_taken, D-023 slice 2; the owner: heavily reduced, not immune). Cold and bleed are the answers, or a Frost ingot beside the fire skill adding cold; it is the first mob that asks the build a question the whelps did not.
Life beyond hostiles (owner, 3 Sep 2026): grazers that bolt when you come near and never bite. Hunting them is a choice, and the hide is the start of a leather line.

elite_modifiers.design_purpose: The anti-Glacier elite: chill never sticks, so the freeze-shatter sentence needs a second answer in the pack (D-016 statuses meet resistance, PoE-style).
The anti-Wildfire elite: it will not burn, and its death is a fire nova - stand back for the kill or eat the burst. Positioning is the counter, as always (D-012).
The anvil: bleeds find no vein and the life pool is a wall. Slow enough to disengage from - fighting it is a choice you commit to.
Pure pressure: faster than you in a straight line. Chill and pits are the counters - the grammar answers what stats cannot.

design_purpose_elites: The bounty (Wave 7 slice 2; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: the world a beat ahead): every crowned kill also rolls its bounty - an Ember Catalyst six times in ten, a Preserving Catalyst four - so the catalysts that temper come mostly off the crowned, and the crowned den in the far rings and the later eras. The families keep their own rare catalyst drops because the typed currency (D-023 slice 3) needs a family's kind to fall from the family. The heartland's mobs hit harder (whelp 6, hound 4, husk 8; Wave 7 slice 2): fewer mobs there now, deadlier when they land, and the train stacks them. Wave 3 elite prefixes: worldgen's danger rings decide who spawns elite (farther out, more often); each interacts with the D-016 status grammar rather than only multiplying numbers, and each pays triple gear/page chance plus an extra loot pass - elites are why you hunt the far rings. Trial rooms do not roll elites yet (the dungeon pass owns that). A family or a prefix may name damage_taken, its share of each packet type (D-023 slice 2); a prefix's share multiplies onto the family's. 0 would be immunity; the owner asked for heavy reductions instead, so builds meet resistance, never a wall.

gathering_sites.design_purpose: Safe early gathering; controls how long shelter and fuel work takes
Iron source with real risk, so open-world death rules matter; reinforcing the mine (order world effect) removes the ambushes

open_world_death.design_purpose: Open-world death drops carried inventory at the site for recovery (D-006); permanent equipment is never dropped

design_purpose_loot: Every mob pays out into the survival economy (fuel, ore, stone) and, since D-023 slice 3, in a KIND: the coin is retired and each family pays the typed currency its nature suggests (currency_kind: the fire families Ember Catalysts, husks and knights Vanguards, hounds and crawlers Quicksilver, the living Marrow), at a chance of its own in its loot table - one each, rarely, because a kind is worth many coins. An elite pays one more of its family's kind on top of its extra passes. Three kinds of entry: {item,min,max,chance} materials; {gear: rarity, tier, chance} a rolled piece on any base (D-014); {skill_page: true, chance} a page teaching one skill the player does not know yet, weighted by skills.json drop_weight (D-016). Page chances are set so a first hour of hunting finds one or two skills; the mob pass will move them onto elites. Stone creatures pay SPLIT stone (D-021): the yard, not the husk, makes masonry. Razor-blade tuning (owner, 4 Sep): the kind rates are first guesses.
design_purpose_pacing: Equal threat, different shape (Wave 8 slice 1; the owner, 4 Sep 2026: a slower mob that hits harder is fine as long as the danger feels the same as the faster hounds, and never a Valheim zone ladder): every family's threat score (combat::threatScore - damage per round, reach, bulk, the verb's control) sits in one band; what differs is the verb (combat_realtime.json behaviours). The lurker came down to 120 life and 6 damage and roots; the knight to 170 and wards; the husk guards; the crawler swarms; the hound harries; the archer marks; the wisps kindle; the shrieker recruits and is the one family under the band on purpose - its threat is who it invites. Long fights (owner, 3 Sep 2026: 'we get too powerful too quick ... more like early MMOs, lots of mobs and it takes a while to kill things', combat should 'start a bit more powerful' - the swing stays, the life bars grow). Mob life is two and a half times the first cut and mob damage seven tenths, player numbers untouched: a day-one whelp takes three heavy blows instead of two-and-a-bit, a pack is a thirty-second fight where spacing and the sweep matter, and the first Keen mace no longer ends era one. The trial's bosses keep their numbers; the oracle (tools/balance) holds their win rates in band.
